```{r setup, message=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(magrittr)
library(knitr)
source("helper_functions/ndar_qc.R")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = F, warning = F)
```

This Rmd cleans the NDAR CDI exports and writes `data/nda_private/cached_data.Rds`.
Everything derived from NDA data goes in `data/nda_private/`, which is gitignored:
the repo is public, and the NDA Data Use Certification forbids redistributing GUIDs or item-level data.

Raw exports go in `data/ASD CDI data/` (`mci_sentences02.txt`, `mci_words_gestures01.txt`).
The QC logic is in `helper_functions/ndar_qc.R`.

# Typically-developing data (Wordbank)

```{r load-wordbank-data}
base::load("data/eng_ws_raw_data.Rds")

d_td_ws <- eng_ws %>%
  mutate(produces = value == "produces") %>%
  filter(!is.na(category)) %>%
  dplyr::select(data_id, produces, age, production, sex,
                ethnicity, mom_ed, category, definition) %>%
  mutate(form = "WS")
```

# ASD data (NDAR)

```{r read-ndar}
ws <- read_ndar("data/ASD CDI data/mci_sentences02.txt")
wg <- read_ndar("data/ASD CDI data/mci_words_gestures01.txt")

ws_items <- ws_item_vars(ws$data)  # 680 vocabulary items
wg_items <- wg_item_vars(wg$data)  # 396 vocabulary items

m_ws <- item_matrix(ws$data, ws_items)
m_wg <- item_matrix(wg$data, wg_items)

dict_ws <- ws_dictionary(ws$desc, ws_items)
dict_wg <- wg_dictionary(wg$desc, wg_items)

stopifnot(all(dict_ws$definition %in% d_td_ws$definition))
```

Loaded `r nrow(ws$data)` WS rows and `r nrow(wg$data)` WG rows.

## Response coding

**WS.** The NDA data dictionary codes each item as 0 = No; 1 = Says & Understands; 2 = Understands; 3 = Says.
The previous version of this script scored any non-zero code as "produces", so "understands only" counted as produced.
Now only codes 1 and 3 count as produced.
(The stored `mcs_vc_total` matches the count of 1s.)

**WG.** The data dictionary says nothing about the codes, and datasets disagree.
Most use 1 = understands, 2 = understands & says, but some (collections 19 and 2027) use 1 = says, 2 = understands only.
For each `dataset_id`, we choose whichever code reproduces the lab's stored "words produced" total (`mcg_vc_totpr`):

```{r wg-coding}
wg_coding <- infer_wg_coding(wg$data, m_wg)
wg_coding %>%
  left_join(distinct(wg$data, dataset_id, collection_id), by = "dataset_id") %>%
  relocate(collection_id) %>% arrange(collection_id) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)

wg_produce_code <- wg_coding$produce_code[match(wg$data$dataset_id, wg_coding$dataset_id)]
wg_produce_code <- replace_na(wg_produce_code, 2L) # datasets w/o usable items; never kept
```

## Administration-level QC

Each row (one CDI administration) is checked for:

- **no item data**: every vocabulary item is blank. Many collections only submitted summary scores.
- **items zero-filled**: every item is 0 even though the lab's stored total is non-zero, or the whole dataset has no non-zero item (e.g. WG collection 1600).
- **items disagree with stored total**: the recomputed production count misses the stored total by more than max(`r QC$total_tol_abs` words, `r 100*QC$total_tol_rel`%). A stored total of 999 is NDA's missing-value code, so those rows can't be checked.
- **incomplete items**: fewer than `r 100*QC$min_completeness`% of items answered. One exception: some labs leave "no" answers blank, so if the answered items reproduce the stored total, blank items are scored as "no" (`blanks_as_no`).
- **identical to another child**: an administration's response vector (with at least `r QC$clone_min_words` words produced) is identical to a different child's.
- **duplicates**: GUID identifies a child. Within a form, several rows with the same GUID × age are the same administration:
  - if their responses are identical, we keep one;
  - if their responses differ, we keep the best-verified, most complete row;
  - if no single row is best, we drop all of them ("conflicting duplicate").
- **age out of range**: WS `r QC$age_ws[1]`–`r QC$age_ws[2]` months; WG `r QC$age_wg[1]`–`r QC$age_wg[2]` months.

These decisions are made per administration, so a clean, non-duplicated child is kept even if their collection has other problems.

```{r qc}
admins <- bind_rows(
  score_admins(ws$data, m_ws, "WS") %>% dedupe_admins(),
  score_admins(wg$data, m_wg, "WG", wg_produce_code) %>% dedupe_admins()
) %>%
  group_by(form) %>% group_modify(~ pick_one_per_child(.x)) %>% ungroup()

admins %>% count(form, exclusion) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = form, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(WS + WG)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Fate of every NDAR row")
```

## Collection trust scores

For each collection we compute:

- **item_coverage**: share of rows with usable item-level data.
- **verification**: share of checkable rows whose items reproduce the stored total.
- **consistency**: 1 minus the share of child × age groups with conflicting versions.
- **coding** (WG only): how well the inferred response coding reproduces the stored totals.

**trust** is the mean of these four, with a missing verification counted as 0.5.
Tiers: A ≥ .85, B ≥ .60, C < .60.
Collections with no usable item data are "summary only": they have stored totals that could still be used for sumscore analyses.

**uniqueness** (distinct child × age / rows) is reported but not included in the score: exact duplicates are harmless once collapsed.
It is still a warning sign about how a collection was submitted (e.g. collection 2024).

```{r trust}
data_sources <- read_csv("data/NDA data sources.csv", show_col_types = F)

trust <- collection_trust(admins, wg_coding) %>%
  left_join(select(data_sources, collection_id, PI), by = "collection_id")

trust %>%
  select(form, collection_id, PI, rows, children, item_coverage, verification,
         consistency, coding, uniqueness, trust, tier, kept_children, kept_admins) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)
```

Analyses should be re-run on tier-A collections only as a sensitivity check.

**Population caveats** (not captured by the score):

- Collection 2024 (Vouloumanos) appears to be infant siblings of children with ASD, not diagnosed children.
- Collection 9 (Courchesne) says normal control data would also be deposited.

`asd_dx_unconfirmed` flags these collections.

```{r flags}
dx_unconfirmed <- c(2024, 9)
admins <- admins %>%
  left_join(select(trust, form, collection_id, trust, tier), by = c("form", "collection_id")) %>%
  mutate(asd_dx_unconfirmed = collection_id %in% dx_unconfirmed)
```

## Item-level data

```{r long}
d_asd_ws <- to_long(filter(admins, form == "WS"), m_ws, dict_ws, "WS")
d_asd_wg <- to_long(filter(admins, form == "WG"), m_wg, dict_wg, "WG", wg_produce_code)

add_meta <- function(d, f) d %>%
  left_join(admins %>% filter(form == f) %>% select(row, tier, trust, asd_dx_unconfirmed), by = "row") %>%
  left_join(select(data_sources, collection_id, collection_title), by = "collection_id")
d_asd_ws <- add_meta(d_asd_ws, "WS")
d_asd_wg <- add_meta(d_asd_wg, "WG")
```

## Item-profile check

The checks above can't catch a lab that mapped responses to the wrong items: totals still agree, and section totals look normal.
This check compares each collection's item-by-item production rates with what TD children of the same vocabulary size produce (Wordbank).

- Real ASD differences are modest and shared across collections.
- A mapping error shows up as many items far off (|observed − expected| > .30) in a pattern that replicates across random halves of the collection's children.
- A collection is flagged when more than 2% of items are that far off **and** the split-half correlation of its residual profile is above .70.
- Flagged collections get `item_profile_ok = FALSE` and tier C: their stored sumscores may be fine, but their item-level data are not.

```{r item-profile}
base::load("data/eng_wg_raw_data.Rds")
td_ref <- list(
  WS = d_td_ws %>% transmute(row = data_id, definition, value = as.integer(produces)),
  WG = eng_wg %>% filter(!is.na(category)) %>%
    transmute(row = data_id, definition, value = as.integer(value == "produces")))
profile <- bind_rows(
  item_profile_check(d_asd_ws %>% filter(one_per_child), td_ref$WS) %>% mutate(form = "WS"),
  item_profile_check(d_asd_wg %>% filter(one_per_child), td_ref$WG) %>% mutate(form = "WG"))

profile %>% select(form, collection_id, profile_admins, gross_items, split_half_r,
                   item_profile_anomaly, worst_items) %>%
  arrange(form, desc(gross_items)) %>% kable(digits = 2)

trust <- trust %>%
  left_join(profile %>% select(form, collection_id, gross_items, split_half_r, item_profile_anomaly),
            by = c("form", "collection_id")) %>%
  mutate(item_profile_ok = !coalesce(item_profile_anomaly, FALSE),
         tier = ifelse(!item_profile_ok, "C", tier)) %>%
  select(-item_profile_anomaly)

upd <- function(d, f) d %>% select(-tier) %>%
  left_join(trust %>% filter(form == f) %>% select(collection_id, tier, item_profile_ok), by = "collection_id")
admins <- admins %>% select(-tier) %>%
  left_join(trust %>% select(form, collection_id, tier, item_profile_ok), by = c("form", "collection_id"))
d_asd_ws <- upd(d_asd_ws, "WS")
d_asd_wg <- upd(d_asd_wg, "WG")
```

Flagged: `r with(filter(trust, !item_profile_ok), paste(form, collection_id, collapse = ", "))`.
Downstream analyses exclude flagged collections by default (`include_flagged` parameter).

# Final dataset stats

```{r final-stats}
bind_rows(d_asd_ws %>% mutate(form = "WS"), d_asd_wg %>% mutate(form = "WG")) %>%
  distinct(form, collection_id, collection_title, tier, row, GUID, one_per_child) %>%
  group_by(form, collection_id, collection_title, tier) %>%
  summarise(administrations = n(), children = n_distinct(GUID), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(form, desc(administrations)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r production-by-age, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
bind_rows(d_asd_ws %>% mutate(form = "WS"), d_asd_wg %>% mutate(form = "WG")) %>%
  group_by(form, row, GUID, age, tier) %>%
  summarise(production = sum(value, na.rm = T), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = production, group = GUID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = .1) + geom_point(aes(color = tier), alpha = .3) +
  facet_wrap(~form, scales = "free") + theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Age (months)", y = "Words produced")
```

# Save data

```{r save}
save(d_asd_wg, d_asd_ws, d_td_ws, admins, trust, wg_coding, profile, QC,
     file = "data/nda_private/cached_data.Rds")
```
